name: SolariNet
tagline: One console for the whole fleet.
positioning: SolariNet is a self-hosted monitoring and control plane that gives a homelab operator one live view of every system, service, and network link across the fleet.
origin: SolariNet grew out of one operator's need to see an entire self-hosted fleet at a glance — dozens of servers, single-board computers, switches, and services scattered across a home network, each with its own dashboard or none at all. Built as a lean standard-C control plane behind a browser dashboard, it treats the homelab the way an NOC treats a datacenter: one console, live telemetry, honest status, and no cloud dependency. Every host is named for an element; the network is the periodic table.

values.statement: Own your infrastructure, and see it clearly.
clauses: Self-hosted by default — no telemetry leaves the fleet, no cloud account gates the view.
Honest status over reassuring green — a degraded link reads as degraded.
Lean and portable — standard C, no runtime to feed, runs where the fleet runs.

principles.title: One console, not a dozen tabs
principles.body: The fleet is shown as a single live surface — hosts, services, links, and alerts — so an operator answers 'what's wrong?' in one glance, not by hunting across a dozen device UIs.

principles.title: The database is the source of record
principles.body: Topology, identity, and config are read from a system of record, not scraped or hand-kept. The dashboard and the DNS zones are rendered views of the same truth.

principles.title: Status is earned, never assumed
principles.body: A node is 'up' because it answered, not because nothing said otherwise. Unknown is its own state, distinct from healthy.

principles.title: Portable over convenient
principles.body: Standard C and plain Makefiles over frameworks; a browser and no build step over a toolchain. It should still compile and run in five years.

marks.useWhen: The default mark — the network-node glyph on the near-black ground. App icon, favicon, cover, and anywhere the brand signs off.
The node glyph alone, no ground, for small sizes and monochrome uses (terminal splash, favicon at 16px).

logo.unit: The mark is a hub-and-spoke network graph: a ringed teal core radiating six spokes to satellite nodes — four teal, two signal-red for alert states — built on the 8px grid.
logo.clearSpace: Keep clear space equal to the core-ring diameter on all sides.
logo.minSize: 24px glyph on screen; 16px favicon glyph without the grid ground.
misuse: Don't recolor the core off SolariNet teal.
Don't drop the mark on a light ground without the dark plate.
Don't add a glow beyond the built-in node bloom.
Don't rotate, skew, or redistribute the spokes.
Don't outline or emboss the nodes.
Don't stretch the mark to non-uniform proportions.

palette.name: SolariNet Teal
palette.role: Accent — core, links, active state, emphasis

palette.name: Ink
palette.role: Body type on the dark ground

typefaces.fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

icons.stroke: 1.8px, round caps and joins, on the 24px grid

imagery.treatment: Dark-UI captures of the live dashboard and topology graphs; grayscale for supporting photography, full color only for the product surface itself.
imagery.sourcePolicy: Product screenshots and rendered topology only — no stock photography.
